title: Parshas Lech Lecha Questions for Kids at the Shabbos Table
description: 15 Parshas Lech Lecha questions for the Shabbos table, sorted by age, each with a short answer for parents. Plus what-would-you-do questions for kids.
keywords: parshas lech lecha shabbos table questions
lech lecha parsha questions and answers
intro:
These Parshas Lech Lecha questions for kids are sorted by age so everyone at the Shabbos table gets a turn: easy ones for the little ones, story questions for the middle children, and thinking questions for the older ones. Each one has a short answer so you are never stuck.

A tip that works at almost every table: let a younger child ask a question to an older sibling, and let the older child answer in their own words before you add the answer here.

sections.heading: Easy Lech Lecha Questions for Little Ones (Ages 3 to 5)
sections.html:
1. Who did Hashem talk to at the start of the parsha?
    Avram, who later becomes Avraham Avinu.
  2. What did Hashem tell Avram to do?
    To leave his home and go to a new land that Hashem would show him.
  3. Who came along with Avram?
    His wife Sarai, his nephew Lot, and the people who learned about Hashem from them.
  4. What did Hashem tell Avram to look up and count?
    The stars. Hashem promised that Avram's children would be as many as the stars.
  5. What new name did Hashem give Avram?
    Avraham. And Sarai became Sarah.

sections.heading: Story Questions for Children Ages 6 to 9
sections.html:
1. Why did Avram go down to Mitzrayim?
    There was a famine in Canaan and no food, and in Mitzrayim there was food. Chazal count the famine as one of Avram's tests, and he did not complain.
  2. Why did Avram and Lot split up?
    Their shepherds were quarreling because there was not enough grass for all the animals. Avram wanted peace, so he let Lot choose where to go first.
  3. Which place did Lot choose, and was it a good choice?
    He chose the green plain near Sedom. The land was rich, but the people were very wicked, so it was not a good place to live.
  4. How many men did Avram take to rescue Lot?
    318 men. With Hashem's help they beat four powerful kings.
  5. What did Avram refuse to take from the king of Sedom?
    Anything at all, not even a thread or a shoelace, so no one could say a person made Avram rich instead of Hashem.

sections.heading: Thinking Questions for Older Children (Ages 10 and Up)
sections.html:
1. Hashem did not tell Avram where he was going. Why might Hashem have kept it a secret?
    The meforshim explain that it made the test greater and Avram's trust more complete. Going somewhere unknown shows you are following Hashem, not the place.
  2. Rashi says lech lecha means "go for yourself, for your good." How can a hard change be for our good?
    Growth often needs us to leave what is comfortable. Avram became Avraham, the father of a nation, only because he left.
  3. Lot chose to live near Sedom. Why did Avram still risk his life to save him?
    Family is family, and a Yid helps another Yid in trouble even when it was their own mistake that put them there.
  4. Why do you think Avram built a mizbeach and called out in Hashem's Name wherever he went?
    To thank Hashem, and to teach everyone around him that there is one Creator. His whole life was about making Hashem known.
  5. Avraham did the bris milah the very same day Hashem commanded it. What does that teach us about doing mitzvos?
    Zerizus: doing a mitzvah eagerly and right away, without pushing it off.

sections.heading: What Would You Do? Lech Lecha Questions That Connect to Your Child's Week
sections.html:
• You are starting in a new class and you do not know anyone yet. What would Avram do? What can you do on the first day?
  • You and your brother both want the same seat in the car. How could you say what Avram said to Lot, "Let there be no quarrel between us"?
  • Your friend made a choice you told them not to make, and now they need help. Do you help? Why?
  • Someone offers you a big prize, but taking it would make people think the wrong thing. Would you still take it?

There are no wrong answers to these. The goal is to hear how your child thinks and to praise every answer that sounds like Avraham Avinu.

sections.heading: How to Keep Your Kids Engaged at the Shabbos Table
sections.html:
Ask one question between each course instead of all of them at once. Children who know another question is coming stay at the table longer.

Let the child who answers choose who gets the next question. Give the hardest question to a parent or guest now and then, so the children get to hear grown ups think out loud too.

If your child learned the parsha in cheder or school this week, ask them to teach the table one thing their rebbi or morah said. Being the teacher is often the part they remember most.

sections.heading: A One-Line Summary of Lech Lecha to Start the Conversation
sections.html:
If you need an opener before the questions: "This week Hashem told Avram to leave everything and go, Avram went without knowing where, and because he trusted Hashem, he became the first father of the Jewish people."

Then ask: "Who can tell me one thing that happened to Avram on the way?"

faq.q: What are good Lech Lecha questions for young kids?
faq.a: Keep them simple and concrete: who did Hashem talk to, what did He tell Avram to do, what did Avram count in the sky, and what was Avram's new name.

faq.q: What is the main lesson of Parshas Lech Lecha for children?
faq.a: Trusting Hashem even when we do not know what comes next, along with keeping peace in the family, helping others, and remembering that everything we have comes from Hashem.

faq.q: How many questions should I ask at the Shabbos table?
faq.a: Three to five is usually plenty. Spread them between courses and let the children ask some of them to each other.

faq.q: Can children write or draw their answers on Shabbos?
faq.a: No. Writing and drawing are melacha, so on Shabbos the questions are for talking only. If your child enjoys drawing the parsha, do it during the week or before Shabbos.
